item.description: A father took several weeks of paternity leave when his second child was born. During that time, he became more confident in his role as primary caregiver and built connections with other parents in his neighbourhood. item.description: Since his retirement in 2012, former FBI agent Dave Benscoter from Washington has been searching for nearly extinct apple varieties in the northwestern United States. item.title: Sycamore Gap tree shows new shoots over a meter tall three years after felling
item.description: Three years after the illegal felling of the famous Sycamore Gap tree at Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland, new aerial photographs reveal that the stump is flourishing. item.description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Dragon capsule 'Grace' has lifted off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida with four crew members for NASA's Crew-13 mission to the international space station. item.title: Bear Backpack wins Fat Bear Week, Google celebrates with animation
item.description: Bear Backpack has won Fat Bear Week, the annual online tournament of Katmai National Park and Reserve in Alaska that has drawn attention to conservation and viewers to the park's livestream cameras since 2014. item.description: In Campbellsville, Kentucky, resident Venitia discovered an Eastern box turtle with a thick layer of bright blue paint on its shell in her new backyard. item.title: Orphaned rhino Chamboi grows up in Kenyan oasis
item.description: On September 6, 2023, rangers from Tsavo Trust and Kenya Wildlife Service found a newborn rhino calf alone in Tsavo West National Park in Kenya. The animal, just one day old and apparently born prematurely, was found hypoglycemic and shivering with no mother nearby. item.description: In Mississippi, April Stewart and her husband, both veterans, have been running the Gulf Coast Primate Sanctuary since October 2024. item.title: Solar train revives ancient Andes route in Argentina
item.description: In the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO World Heritage valley in Argentina's Jujuy province, the Tren Solar de la Quebrada has been running since June 2024 — Latin America's first solar-powered train. item.title: Stolen Greek antiquities returned to Greece after 5,000 years
item.description: New York has returned 15 ancient Greek artworks worth millions of dollars to Greece. The pieces, including two bronze helmets, bronze breastplates, a marble bust of a Roman emperor and a terracotta vessel, were discovered at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. item.title: Chinese reactor achieves nuclear fusion with hydrogen-boron
item.description: Chinese engineers have achieved sustained nuclear fusion for the first time using hydrogen-boron as fuel, a much cleaner and more abundant alternative to the conventional deuterium-tritium mixture. The state-backed ENN Group used a laser and radio waves to generate plasma in a spherical tokamak reactor. In the process, a hydrogen proton and a boron-11 nucleus fuse into harmless helium nuclei...

item.title: Social innovator Ken Banks: listening makes better leaders
item.description: Social innovator Ken Banks writes that listening is an underestimated leadership skill. After more than thirty years of work in nature conservation, international development and technology, he discovered that the best lessons did not come from offering solutions, but from realizing that the original question was wrong. item.title: Snow leopard cub Sarka born at Bronx Zoo
item.description: A female snow leopard cub has been born at the Bronx Zoo in New York on May 31, as the daughter of parents Dariga and Moutig. The cub, named Sarka (Nepali for 'shark'), passed her medical examinations and vaccinations and is now exploring the Himalayan Highlands habitat of the zoo alongside her mother. item.title: Music education linked to lower school absenteeism in Rhode Island
item.description: A new study by Quadrant Research, commissioned by the Rhode Island State Council on the Arts, shows that students who take music lessons for four years are chronically absent from school less often. item.title: Horizon Europe receives €500 million extra for research and innovation
item.description: The European Commission has released an additional €500 million for Horizon Europe, the EU's research and innovation programme, for 2026 and 2027. This brings the budget for these two years to approximately €14.8 billion. item.title: Red-legged frog returns to Yosemite after 50-year absence
item.description: About fifty years ago, the red-legged frog disappeared from Yosemite National Park, due in part to habitat loss, invasive American bullfrogs, and an increase in raccoons. Park staff removed the bullfrogs and restored wetlands and riverbanks. item.description: Media outlet The Bulwark held a live show in Springfield, Ohio on September 25, with all proceeds going to the Haitian Support Center. item.title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library doubles reach in London
item.description: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which has been sending free books to children under five since 1995, is expanding in London. The programme is growing from five to ten of London's 32 boroughs, enabling 157,000 additional children to receive a free book each month. item.title: Olive ridley sea turtles nest for first time on US West Coast
item.description: For the first time, olive ridley sea turtles have been spotted nesting on the American West Coast. A female laid eggs at Seal Beach, and three days later another did the same at Huntington Beach. Scientist Lindsey Peavey Reeves called it unexpected. item.description: On the English coast, National Trust golf course Sandilands in Lincolnshire, purchased in 2020, has been transformed into a wetland nature reserve the size of 45 football pitches.
